subject.title: [bug]：Gateway pairing failure on Trim OS / TerraMaster NAS: WebSocket closes with code 1002 during device proof response

question: Should OpenClaw support a documented Trim OS loopback/private-deployment pairing recovery path, and if so should it live in core gateway auth, the Trim OS package manager, or device CLI documentation?
rationale: The reporter’s workaround request would change or document a gateway auth bypass/config behavior, and the current evidence does not prove whether the failing 1002 is client protocol drift, malformed connect params, or package-managed config regeneration.

options.title: Diagnose protocol and package behavior first
options.body: Collect sanitized connect-frame/protocol numbers, gateway logs, installed client/gateway versions, and the Trim OS config generator owner before changing auth behavior.

options.title: Document existing device pairing only
options.body: Keep the auth model unchanged and answer with the current devices command/protocol docs if the logs show an outdated or incompatible client package.

options.title: Design a supported package recovery path
options.body: If private loopback deployments need auth relaxation, require an explicit maintainer-approved secure package/doctor path rather than manual gateway.auth deletion.

recommendation.title: Diagnose protocol and package behavior first
recommendation.body: Collect sanitized connect-frame/protocol numbers, gateway logs, installed client/gateway versions, and the Trim OS config generator owner before changing auth behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is around gateway pairing/auth protocol documentation and device-token CLI behavior.
